title: User-Centered Design
summary: User-centered design makes user tasks and evidence authoritative while treating business and technical constraints as explicit inputs.

MUST.text: Write research questions before choosing methods.
Recruit people who represent the real task and context.
Trace major decisions to findings, constraints or labeled hypotheses.

SHOULD.text: Use formative research early and summative evaluation after design stabilizes.
Include assistive technology in relevant research scenarios.

AVOID.text: Ask leading questions to validate a preferred solution.
Treat stakeholder approval as proof of usability.

DECIDE.decision: Interview or observe users in context

FAILURE_MODES: Recruiting people who do not match the real task or context produces findings that do not transfer.
Leading questions validate a preferred solution instead of revealing user needs.
Summative metrics without formative insight leave the cause of failure unexplained.

sources.title: ISO 9241-210:2019 Human-centred design for interactive systems
Nielsen Norman Group — When to Use Which User-Experience Research Methods
